extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities, state/local governments, non-profits, and other stakeholders who want to track or participate in EPA rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for finding, tracking, and submitting input on EPA regulations (where they are published, how they become codified, and the official channels for commenting and accessing dockets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority and nature of regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is called a regulatory agency because Congress authorizes us to write regulations that explain the technical, operational, and legal details necessary to implement laws. Regulations are mandatory requirements that can apply to individuals, businesses, state or local governments, non-profit institutions, or others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations implement statutes and create binding obligations for covered parties; understand that regs carry legal force and are not optional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between the Federal Register (FR) and the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register (FR) is the official daily publication for rules, proposed rules, and notices of federal agencies and organizations. There's a difference between the CFR and the FR. The FR announces ongoing activities of the agencies and notifies you when you can comment on a proposed regulation. Once a final decision is issued in the form of a final regulation, the regulation is then codified when it is incorporated into the CFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FR to learn about proposed rules and comment periods; use the CFR to read the codified, final regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title 40, Code of Federal Regulations (40 CFR) coverage and update timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations are codified annually in the U.S. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). Title 40: Protection of Environment is the section of the CFR that deals with EPA's mission of protecting human health and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that Title 40 is typically not updated until July of the current calendar year; for official, codified requirements consult the CFR (available from the Government Printing Office).

rubrics_metrics.name: e-CFR as an up-to-date unofficial CFR
rubrics_metrics.description: e-CFR: an up-to-date, unofficial version of the CFR available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you need current-effective regulatory text between annual CFR updates, consult the e-CFR for a more current (but unofficial) view of codified regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Regulations.gov as the official online comment system
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations.gov: This multi-agency website serves as an online clearinghouse for materials related to EPA rulemakings and is EPA's official on-line comment system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments via Regulations.gov and access rules published in the Federal Register and related documents there; Regulations.gov is the primary portal for public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA docket centers as alternative access and submission points
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Docket Centers provide access to the same information as Regulations.gov for those people without access to the Internet. In addition, the docket centers provide access to those pieces of information that we are unable to provide electronically. You may also submit comments to the docket centers, in addition to submitting them via Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot use Regulations.gov or need materials not posted online, visit or use an EPA docket center; docket centers can receive submissions and house source documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agendas and Regulatory Plans as tracking tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory Agendas and Regulatory Plans: Download twice yearly publications of EPA's regulatory activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these twice-yearly publications to monitor upcoming and planned EPA rulemakings and to identify when new proposals may be coming that you might want to review or comment on.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to find regulatory information by topic, industry sector, region, or state
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic outlines of where regulations apply: regulatory information by environmental topic or regulatory information by industry sector. EPA has ten Regional offices, each of which is responsible for several states and territories. Get information about your Region or your state's environmental agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search EPA resources by topic or sector, or consult your EPA Region or state environmental agency for localized applicability and implementation details; many state agencies administer federal regulations and provide permitting and compliance assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gateway to State-by-State Resource Locators (state-level resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gateway to State-by-State Resource Locators, sponsored by EPA's Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assistance, provides access to state-by-state environmental regulations, compliance assistance, and where applicable, permits and forms for a variety of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For state-specific requirements, forms, and compliance help, use the Gateway to connect with state resources—federal requirements are often administered at the state level and state rules or permits may also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to provide input before finalization
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA rulemakings (i.e., regulations that are under development) could impact you once they become final regulations. You have an opportunity to provide input on almost every regulation before it is finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay informed via the FR, Regulations.gov, regulatory agendas, and regional/state resources so you can submit comments during the public comment period and influence rule development where appropriate.
